name: Construction & Management Sim
description: Zone it, staff it, and find out what you got wrong three tiers later. The pack's stance is that a city builder is a feedback loop wearing a map: nothing here places buildings for the player, and every structure that appears did so because world.zone_planner's growth rules were satisfied by demand the citizens themselves generated. That is why the agents come before the advisors -- world.citizen_agent_sim produces the home-work-shop traffic that ui.demand_indicators reads, so the RCI bars are a measurement rather than a script. Disasters are deliberately separate and optional: a management sim whose difficulty comes from random destruction is hiding a shallow economy behind an event.
loop: zone/place → citizens arrive → balance economy → unlock tier

signatureCompound.name: Demand Builds a Block
signatureCompound.description: The loop in one block: zone_planner marks a residential parcel, citizen_agent_sim's agents want somewhere to live and generate demand, demand_indicators turns that into an RCI reading and an advisory, service_coverage decides whether power and water actually reach the parcel, and only then does a building appear. Nothing in that chain is scripted, which is why the same four components produce both a boom and a slum.
